coverage_notes: 46 features covering usage accounting, provider meters/accounts, telemetry and analytics, metrics logs, current-run projections, health/forensics, logging, build gate, admission, process/pause containment, workspaces (provisioning, ownership, remote, warm base), sandbox (Codex policy and --test harness), upgrade, init, env, boot plumbing, rtk, dev tooling, utilities and the durable state layout. Totals: lib_loc 61494 (snapshot src/lib at 3339b88 plus src/priv and engine-shell lines counted from `git show 3339b88` where noted), test_loc 51833, loc_saving_estimate 35462. Usage sources: 39 retained run dirs in ~/.aiur/logs (2026-09-15..09-26: telemetry.ndjson, alerts.ndjson, boot.out.log, 3 debug aiur.log); 14 instance state dirs in ~/.config/aiur (the engine's AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR default); ~/.aiur/repo/*/*/{executor wake streams, analytics, github-quota, meta}; ~/.aiur/build-gate; 7 real configs (~/.aiur/config, config.archon, repo-local aiur, archon, kevinweaver-dev, <private repo> (private) (private), <private repo> (private) (private)) parsed with Ruby YAML for key names only; 68,609 Executor tool uses extracted from 1,190 transcript files under ~/.claude/projects/-home-user-github-everdred-* (split into operational vs code-reading commands by a regex that drops src/lib, tests, worktrees, diffs; this research session excluded); 6,534 Codex sessions and 1,123 Claude agent transcripts grepped with fixed strings/regex. Limits: Claude transcripts only go back to 2026-09-01 and run logs to 2026-09-15, so older use (July-August) is invisible except through git history, wake streams and meta logs. Features whose code is shared with other surfaces are attributed here by primary owner: dispatch_policy.ex lines 1-605 only (admission); Claude OTLP receiver (claude/telemetry.ex etc.) left to the agent-backend surface; dashboard presenters/LiveViews that read these subsystems left to the web surface; `aiur upgrade`, `aiur usage`, `aiur analytics` and `aiur init` as commands are also CLI-surface items - here they are listed for the machinery behind them. Test LOC is by file-name match plus a scan for test files referencing each module >=3 times; a few mixed files (dispatch_policy_test.exs, workspace_and_config_test.exs) are attributed whole. Private-repo configs are reported as counts only.

features.name: Run telemetry recorder (writer, resource sampler, lifecycle events, retention)
features.description: Daemon-owned NDJSON stream <run-log>/log/telemetry.ndjson: lifecycle phase events per ticket attempt (dispatch, prewarm, workspace_setup, workspace_ownership, agent_spinup, implement, build_test, review_pause, pr_opened, pr_merged, comment_received), procfs resource samples of daemon and agent process trees, sampler warnings, capacity holds, firehose polls, restarts; size/age retention and segment roll.
entry_points: Aiur.RunTelemetry.Lifecycle.record/5 (13 call sites in orchestrator, agent_runner, workspace/provisioner, coding_agent)
config: observability.telemetry_enabled, telemetry_retention_max_bytes (64 MiB), telemetry_retention_max_age_days (30), telemetry_retention_prune_interval_bytes
features.usage_evidence: Fires in every run: 34 of 39 retained run dirs (~/.aiur/logs/*/log/telemetry.ndjson, 2026-09-15..09-26) hold 454 MB. Record census (python over all files): 457,706 kind=resource, 434,147 kind=warning (243,151 ticket_roots_unavailable + 191,003 resource_sample_warning), 17,880 lifecycle, 3,247 firehose_poll, 42 restart, 9 capacity_hold, 7 capacity_resumed. So 97.6% of records are resource samples or sampler warnings; lifecycle is 2%. Largest file 57 MB, all under the 64 MiB cap (retention works). Consumers: the Executor reads the raw file directly (grep 'telemetry.ndjson' in Executor tool uses, excluding code-reading commands: 93 commands in 25 transcript files, mostly dispatch/lifecycle/resource greps); 14 Codex agent sessions also read it; the /analytics dashboard page (via subsystems-02) is observed in 79 of 173 aiur-team meta files. merged-fixes area N: run_telemetry/writer.ex touched by 4 daemon-stability fixes.
features.rationale: Lifecycle phase timings are the one dataset the Executor actually greps, and they are cheap. The procfs sampler and its warnings produce ~98% of the bytes and nearly all of the noise (ticket_roots_unavailable fires every sample for every ticket whose workspace is not running). Keep the lifecycle writer + retention; cut per-process procfs sampling to a coarse host sample (load/mem) or drop it, and never persist per-sample warnings.
features.rewrite_notes: Remove Procfs (312) and most of Sampler (841); keep Writer + Retention with one schema. Emit warnings as counters in a periodic summary record, not one line per miss. Consider making lifecycle events the only telemetry and deriving capacity/firehose facts from them.

features.name: Telemetry reporting: dataset reducer, run summaries, HTML dashboard generator, timeline, GitHub enricher, `aiur analytics` CLI
features.description: Elixir reducers over telemetry.ndjson: Dataset.build, Summaries.materialize (writes ~/.aiur/repo/<o>/<r>/analytics/runs/<boot>/run-summary.json), a self-contained HTML dashboard generator (mix aiur.telemetry.dashboard) with a GitHub-events enricher and timeline, and the `aiur analytics` CLI that reuses the dashboard Analytics presenter.
features.usage_evidence: run-summary.json materialized 21 times in total (find ~/.aiur/repo -path '*analytics/runs/*' -name run-summary.json, excluding latest/): 20 for aiur-team/aiur, 1 for architecture-docs, 0 for khala despite 20 retained khala run dirs; newest 2026-09-21. `aiur analytics` CLI: 0 Executor invocations in retained transcripts (regex 'aiur(dev)? analytics' over 68,609 Executor tool uses), 5 Codex agent sessions executing it (rg over ~/.codex/sessions exec 'cmd' fields; agents building the feature). mix aiur.telemetry.dashboard: 3 Executor mentions, all while reviewing code, 0 operational. The /analytics page that consumes Dataset/Summaries is captured in 79 of 173 aiur-team meta files (analytics.png); a meta note records its spend panel as 'genuinely absent' usage.
features.rationale: One reader matters (the /analytics page). The portable HTML dashboard, its GitHub enricher, the timeline, the mix task and the `aiur analytics` CLI have no operational use in the retained window and duplicate what the page shows. Summaries also duplicates the Python reducer (subsystems-03).
features.rewrite_notes: Keep Dataset + Summaries (~1,700 lines) feeding the page; delete Dashboard (619), GitHubEnricher (335), Timeline (90), the mix task (150) and AnalyticsCLI (320). If a CLI is wanted, print the same summary JSON the page reads.

features.name: Analytics Python toolkit (analytics/: reduce, run-summary, build-report, cost-report, flake-report)
features.description: Offline Python reducer and report scripts over telemetry NDJSON with a JSON schema; cost-report shells into mix aiur.cost_report; flake-report is a stub that exits with 'not shipped'.
features.usage_evidence: Executor tool uses matching 'analytics/(run-summary|reduce|build-report|cost-report|flake-report)': 4, all in one 2026-08-22 code-review session (reading reduce.py, running its unit tests); 0 operational runs. Codex agent sessions executing 'analytics/run-summary': 0 (rg over ~/.codex/sessions exec cmd fields). Claude agent transcripts mentioning 'analytics/run-summary': 0 of 1,123 files. git: 2 commits (2026-08-09, 08-23).
features.rationale: Unused in every source searched, and it is a second implementation of the Elixir Summaries reducer (the README's 'one reducer' claim is false: Summaries.materialize also writes run-summary.json). flake-report ships as a stub.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete the directory; keep run-summary.v1.json (108 lines) as the documented contract if the summary format survives.

features.name: Usage envelope and headless usage adapters (token accounting intake)
features.description: Provider-neutral UsageEnvelope contract (codec, exact-money, relationship registry) and per-backend adapters that turn Codex turn/thread usage, Claude request usage, DeepSeek/Kimi/OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible responses and Claude OTLP usage into envelopes for the ledger; TokenUsage display helpers.
features.docs: none found in website/docs-app beyond configuration.md pricing keys
features.usage_evidence: 18,589 envelopes accepted across 10 non-empty instance ledgers (~/.config/aiur/<key>/<repo>/usage-ledger/segments/00000001.ndjson; 4 more instance dirs are empty smoke/test shells). By source: codex turn usage 7,164, claude request usage 5,400, codex thread usage 4,892, deepseek request usage 1,133; kimi, open_router and generic openai-compat adapters: 0 records. Coverage: 18,414 (99.1%) have delta.cost=null; 18,589 (100%) carry coverage_reason missing_trusted_occurrence_time; 17,456 (94%) unknown_account_generation. Months: Jul 3,079, Aug 4,120, Sep 11,390.
features.rationale: Token capture is real and continuous, but the envelope carries ~30 fields of provenance (relationship revisions, counter epochs, account generations, exact-money) that end up null or 'unknown' on almost every record. Codex emits two record streams (turn usage and thread usage). Three adapters have never produced a record.
features.rewrite_notes: One record per turn: {run, ticket, attempt, backend, model, input, cached_input, output, reasoning, observed_at}. Drop RelationshipRegistry (458), ExactMoney (261), Compatibility, one of the two Codex streams, and the Kimi/OpenRouter adapters until a config uses them.

features.name: Usage ledger (canonical crash-safe raw usage store)
features.description: Single-writer append-only ledger with idempotency/counter checkpoint, counter policy, retired floor, recovery and quarantine; publishes ordered deltas to the aggregate.
features.usage_evidence: Written in 10 of 14 instance dirs: segment files 0.3-5.8 MB (718-2,553 records each), checkpoint.json ~1.0 MB each. Readers: only UsageAggregate.Store (grep 'Aiur.UsageLedger.' over src/lib: usage_aggregate/store.ex and usage/headless/emitter.ex). Executor reads of usage-ledger files: 7 commands in 2 transcript files, both 2026-09-26 research; git: 2 commits (2026-07-17).
features.rationale: A durable ledger for data whose cost is null 99% of the time does not need its own recovery/quarantine/counter-policy machinery. Merge ledger, aggregate (subsystems-06) and compaction (subsystems-07) into one append-only usage log with an in-memory rollup rebuilt on boot.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep an NDJSON append + fsync; drop CounterPolicy (396), Recovery (470), RetiredFloor, Checkpoint quarantine. Use the shared durable-log helper proposed in subsystems-45.

features.name: Usage aggregate projection (queryable rollup of the ledger)

entry_points: Aiur.UsageAggregate.Query (via Usage.GroupedScopes, BuildOrder usage_runtime, mix aiur.cost_report)
features.usage_evidence: usage-aggregate/checkpoint.json present in 10 instance dirs (22-247 KB). The dashboard Analytics page it feeds is observed in 79/173 meta files.
features.rationale: Same data as the ledger, projected once more with its own checkpoint/recovery/degraded marker. Fold into subsystems-05's rollup.
features.rewrite_notes: A map keyed by {run, ticket, model} rebuilt from the log on boot replaces Store/Checkpoint/Recovery/Key.

features.name: Usage compaction (retention of the usage ledger into compacted blocks)
features.description: Coordinator, policy, floor and manifest for dimension-preserving compaction of old ledger data into blocks.
features.usage_evidence: find ~/.config/aiur -path '*usage-compaction*' -type f | wc -l = 0: the directory (and blocks/) exists in 11 instance dirs but no block or manifest was ever written. git: 1 commit (2026-07-17). Executor mentions: 3 commands, 2 files, 2026-09-26 research only.

features.rewrite_notes: Delete. If growth ever matters, rotate the usage log by month.

features.name: Pricing: price table, pricing windows, grouped usage scopes, cost report tasks
features.description: Versioned per-provider price table with effective-date windows and validator, component/dimension pricing, GroupedScopes cost rollups for the dashboard, and mix aiur.cost_report / aiur.pricing_window.
features.usage_evidence: Priced records: 175 of 18,589 ledger records (0.9%) carry a cost (all others cost=null). mix aiur.cost_report: 0 Executor operational runs, 7 Codex agent sessions (development). pricing_window: 11 Executor mentions, all code work, 0 operational. Meta note (aiur-team meta): Analytics 'reports run-scoped usage telemetry (genuinely absent)'. Fix #1978 (effective-date DeepSeek repricing).
features.rationale: The machinery prices almost nothing because upstream records lack trusted time and account; the cost shown to the Executor comes from provider meters (subsystems-10), not from here.
features.rewrite_notes: A static model->price map and one multiply at read time; drop windows, validator, provider dimensions, property tests, both mix tasks.

features.name: Provider account generation (opaque account identity for usage and meters)
features.description: Owner/registry/lifecycle/tombstones minting opaque local 'account generations' per provider auth binding, with per-backend context modules for Claude, Codex and OpenAI-compatible backends.
features.usage_evidence: Of 18,589 usage envelopes, 17,456 (94%) record account_generation {health: unavailable, reason: owner_unavailable}; only the 1,133 DeepSeek (openai-compatible) records are 'healthy'. git: 3 commits (07-15..08-09).
features.rationale: Built to key usage and meters by account without storing account ids; in practice the owner is unavailable for Codex and Claude, so the field is 'unknown' on nearly every record and pricing then refuses to price.
features.rewrite_notes: Key usage by backend + configured credential name. Delete ProviderAccountGeneration.* and the three backend context modules.

features.name: Provider meters (plan/credit balance meters and `aiur usage`)
features.description: Canonical provider-neutral account meter store/reconciler, projection and refresh; Claude usage API, Codex rate-limit windows, OpenAI-compatible meter probe and OpenRouter credits; ProviderMeterProbe runs a 'usage-probe' in a workspace; `aiur usage` prints it.

Meta checks: 'meter' in 30 of 173 aiur-team meta files (e.g. Units 'Claude tile: 82% - reset time passed'). Executor mentions of provider meter code/state: 7 operational commands in 2 files. OPENROUTER_MANAGEMENT_KEY documented for the credits meter.

features.name: Model availability ledger (model-usage.json) for rate-limit fallback and provider gate

The file is written into the tracked repo: .aiur/model-usage.json has 5 commits on main and shows ' M' in the live checkout's git status; the Executor ran 'git checkout -- .aiur/model-usage.json' 15 times to clean it (grep over Executor tool uses), and mentions the file in 36 operational commands in 10 files. agent.switch_model_on_ratelimit set in 1 of 7 real configs (private).

features.name: Current-run membership store

features.name: Daemon death forensics: crash-dump capture, BEAM-death watchdog, lifecycle journal, launcher self-halt watchdog
features.description: Engine exports ERL_CRASH_DUMP into the run log dir, baselines the dump identity, and a disowned watchdog writes aiur.crash, a per-instance .last-crash marker and a system.beam.crash_dump alert on unexpected BEAM death; DaemonLifecycle journals start/stop to executor/<repo>.control-lifecycle.json; LauncherWatchdog self-halts a detached BEAM whose operator left.
entry_points: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh: aiur_crash_marker_path(1558), crash_dump_identity(1572), new_completed_crash_dump_slogan(1582), write_crash_dump_alert(1592), record_new_crash_dump_alert(1613), record_beam_crash(1627), start_beam_death_watchdog(1795), ERL_CRASH_DUMP export (~878-900)
features.usage_evidence: Retained window: aiur.crash files in ~/.aiur/logs: 0 of 39 dirs; system.beam.crash_dump alerts: 0; erl_crash.dump under ~/.aiur/logs: 0; .last-crash markers in ~/.config/aiur: 1 (2026-07-28). Meanwhile 42 erl_crash.dump files sit in repo roots and worktrees (find <local-checkouts>/everdred ~/.aiur -maxdepth 6 -name erl_crash.dump), all short-lived control/boot BEAMs dying at boot ('nodistribution', 'badarg during boot'), which the capture does not route. control-lifecycle.json journals exist for 6 repos (khala 229 KB); Executor read them 14 times.
features.rationale: Keep the dump path export and one crash marker; the dump-identity baselining and slogan diffing are elaborate for zero captures, and the stray dumps show the real gap is control BEAMs, not the daemon.
features.rewrite_notes: Set ERL_CRASH_DUMP for every BEAM the launcher starts (or disable dumps for control nodes); write one crash marker; keep the lifecycle journal.

features.description: BASH_ENV hook + detached Python lease holder + command wrapper limit concurrent agent mix/elixir builds to agent.max_concurrent_builds, with start stagger, free-memory floor, max hold, retain window; shim entrypoints for non-bash shells; daemon hold-timeout alert monitor; status reads advisory records.
modules: src/priv/build_gate_command_wrapper.bash (counted from git show 3339b88; not in the snapshot copy)
entry_points: config: agent.max_concurrent_builds (default 4), build_start_stagger_seconds, min_free_memory_mb, build_gate_max_hold_seconds, build_gate_retain_seconds, mix_scheduler_cap
features.usage_evidence: On by default for every repo (max_concurrent_builds default 4; set explicitly in 2 of 7 configs). ~/.aiur/build-gate holds 25,454 leaked per-lease temp files = 4,242 lease sessions (4,191 in Aug, 51 in Sep, 1 since 09-19) never cleaned. build_test lifecycle events: 2,720 in retained telemetry. Codex agent sessions mention aiur_build_gate 36,485 times (hook output), 15 Claude agent transcripts show AIUR_BUILD_GATE. Executor: 69 operational commands in 15 files; 31 of 173 aiur-team meta files mention it ('Build-gate leak verified three times this hour, cleared three times'). merged-fixes 2.18: 6 slot-leak fixes in 6 days (#1000..#2401). system.build_gate.hold_timeout alerts in retained ledgers: 0.
features.rationale: Limiting concurrent compiles is needed on one host, but 4,285 lines of bash/python/Elixir lease machinery leaked slots repeatedly and leaks temp files. An flock-per-slot wrapper does the same job.
features.rewrite_notes: `aiur build-slot -- <cmd>` using flock on N lock files (kernel releases on death, no holder process, no retain window); drop BASH_ENV hook, holder.py, HoldMonitor, stagger and memory floor (admission covers memory).

features.name: Host-load admission / load governor (dispatch gates and capacity binding)
features.description: Dispatch-time gates on 1-min load per scheduler, CPU headroom, MemAvailable, file descriptors, BEAM run queue, build status, provider and GitHub quota; AIMD load envelope with cold-start seed, ramp and cooldown; CapacityBinding names the binding constraint; emits system.fleet.capacity.* and system.dispatch.capacity_starved.
modules: lib/aiur/orchestrator/dispatch_policy.ex (lines 1-605 of 1,213; the rest is dispatch ordering, owned by the orchestrator surface)
entry_points: config: agent.max_load_average (default 1.5), target_load_average, load_ramp_step, load_cooldown_seconds, run_queue_threshold, min_free_memory_mb
features.usage_evidence: Executor wake streams (~/.aiur/repo/*/*/executor/*.executor.wakes.ndjson, 9,774 wakes): system.fleet.capacity.starved 1,727 (needs_attention), system.dispatch.capacity_starved 567, fleet.capacity.resumed 399, fleet.capacity.backoff 242, resolved 233 - 3,171 capacity wakes. Telemetry capacity_hold 9 / capacity_resumed 7. max_load_average set in 3 of 7 configs (default on for all); AIMD keys (target_load_average, load_ramp_step, load_cooldown_seconds) only in kevinweaver-dev (1 of 7). The Executor also checks load itself (loadavg/uptime) in 433 operational commands in 73 files. merged-fixes 2.18: load gate not applied or latched, 7 fixes, #2564 open (admission is per daemon).
features.rationale: Admission is necessary on a shared host and fires constantly, but six gates plus an AIMD controller produced a latching/stale-sample bug chain and a wake flood. The Executor still watches load by hand.
features.rewrite_notes: One host-wide admission check (load per core + MemAvailable) shared by all daemons on the host (fixes #2564); drop AIMD envelope, fd and run-queue gates; make capacity events edge-triggered with a minimum dwell to stop wake floods.

features.name: Agent resource guard (trim synthetic load generators)
features.description: Watches registered agent process roots and kills known load-generator descendants (yes/stress) above a cap.
features.usage_evidence: Active by default (synthetic_load_process_cap null = cores/4; the key appears only as a commented template line in the home config and 12 of 12 home-config backups, uncommented in 0 of 7 configs). Trims observed: 0 log lines mentioning resource_guard/synthetic load in retained aiur.log/boot.out.log. git: 1 commit (2026-06-23).
features.rationale: Guards against one historical agent behaviour; no trims observed.

features.name: Process reaper and shutdown cleanup
features.description: Central registry of agent OS pids, process groups and tmux panes, reaped at shutdown in kind order; pidfd-based reap helper; engine-side reaping of stale agents by workspace cwd; ProcessIdentity liveness probe; Shutdown chokepoint deletes opencode sessions.
features.usage_evidence: ticket.N.agent.orphan_reaped alerts: 113 and agent.startup_orphan_claim_released: 92 across retained alert ledgers. merged-fixes 2.17: process reaping recurred (#426/#458/#501 -> #2080 -> #2179 -> #2391, #2406 open, PID reuse).
features.rationale: Necessary; the recurrence chain comes from tracking pids by hand in three places (BEAM registry, pidfd helper, engine shell).
features.rewrite_notes: Launch each agent in its own process group (or systemd scope/cgroup) and kill the group; one registry in the BEAM, no shell-side reaping.

features.name: Pause containment (agent process-group registration for pause/stop)
features.description: Registers each agent's root pid and process group with a generation; confirm/release/paused? during cooperative pause; liveness polling.
features.usage_evidence: Registered at every agent spawn (6 call-site modules). Retained daemon logs contain 71 containment lines, all 'Orchestrator ignored message: {:pause_containment_runtime, ...}' - the runtime notification has no handler.
features.rationale: A second pid/pgid registry beside ProcessReaper; its runtime message is dropped by the orchestrator.
features.rewrite_notes: Fold into the process-group registry of subsystems-30.

features.name: Workspace provisioning (create, hooks, checkout, git metadata, refresh, reconstruction, removal)
features.description: Per-issue workspace lifecycle under <workspace.root>/<repo>/<issue>: provisioner, after_create/before_run/before_remove hooks, PR-anchored checkout, .git-writable metadata, refresh, reconstruction, removal, host lock.
features.usage_evidence: Telemetry: 1,154 workspace_setup and 1,078 agent_spinup lifecycle events in the retained window; census: 823 distinct ticket workspaces, 26 GB on disk; hooks_file set in 7 of 7 configs. merged-fixes area K: 56 fix PRs (workspace.ex 12, agent_environment 8).
features.rationale: Core. The complexity (reconstruction, refresh, git-metadata repair) accreted from fixes; remote-worker and warm-base branches (subsystems-34/35) inflate it.
features.rewrite_notes: Local-only provisioning: clone (or worktree) + hooks + one validated writable .git capability; drop remote clauses.

features.name: Workspace ownership, cleanup and orphaned-worker reaping
features.description: Ownership guardian/store/receipts/reconciler/waiter prevent two workers from using one workspace; WorkspaceCleanup removes workspaces of closed tickets; OrphanedWorkers releases claims whose owner died.
features.usage_evidence: 1,772 workspace_ownership lifecycle events in retained telemetry. 36 workspace-ownership.receipts.corrupt-* files across instance dirs (18 in one aiur instance) plus stray .tmp files; live receipts are usually 45 bytes (empty). orphan_reaped alerts: 113. 'ownership' appears in 76 meta/handoff files (manual lock recovery). Executor operational commands on ownership state: 1.
features.rationale: Needed, but receipts corrupt routinely and recovery is manual.
features.rewrite_notes: flock on <workspace>/.aiur-owner held by the worker process; the kernel releases it on death. Drop Guardian (759), receipts Store, Waiter, Reconciler.

features.name: Remote SSH workers and Docker bootstrap image
features.description: Run workspaces and agents on worker.ssh_hosts over SSH, and seed warm caches from workspace.bootstrap_image via docker.
features.usage_evidence: worker.ssh_hosts set (uncommented) in 0 of 7 real configs; it appears only as the commented template line '# worker: { ssh_hosts: [] ... }' in the home config and 12 of 12 backups. workspace.bootstrap_image in 0 of 7 configs and 0 of 12 backups. The worker_host parameter is threaded through 57 lib files (grep -rl worker_host); matches of worker_host|ssh_hosts|SSH.|Remote. per file: provisioner 57, session_lifecycle 55, dispatcher 45, agent_runner 45, workspace.ex 40.
features.rationale: No configuration uses it, yet it forks every workspace and agent path into local/remote clauses.
features.rewrite_notes: 362 lines of modules plus an estimated ~550 lines of worker_host clauses across 57 files. If remote execution returns, do it as a separate runner package.

features.name: Repo base warm checkout and prewarm (warm-base materialization and dispatch gate)
features.description: RepoBase keeps a pre-compiled base checkout at ~/.aiur/repo/<o>/<r>/latest so workspaces materialize copy-on-write; prewarm detects/runs the base build; the dispatcher holds the fleet while the base is building (system.dispatch.prewarm_blocked). RepoBase also exports the per-repo state path helpers (repo_path/builds_path) used by 22 files.
entry_points: DispatchPolicy.prewarm_gate + dispatcher prewarm hold (~150 lines in orchestrator/dispatcher.ex)
features.usage_evidence: prewarm.enabled=true in 2 of 7 configs (aiur, kevinweaver-dev). Retained telemetry prewarm events: 22 materialize starts, 9 success, 13 materialize_failed -> cold fallback (59% failure), 430 'existing' skips, 89 'disabled'. aiur Executor wake stream: 1,015 system.dispatch.prewarm_blocked wakes between 2026-08-18 and 08-24. merged-fixes 2.17: 5-fix chain (#441, #571, #1555, #2274, #2434), disabled in #2242 (two starts stalled with 31 ready tickets and 0 agents), later re-enabled. Executor: 36 operational commands in 8 files. Note: pre_warmed_sessions (opencode pane prewarm, 7/7 configs) is a different feature owned by the TUI/opencode surface.
features.rationale: Materialization fails more often than it succeeds, the gate has halted the whole fleet, and it produced the largest single wake flood. A per-workspace cold clone plus a shared deps/_build cache is simpler.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete warm-base build, prewarm gate and init prewarm step; keep repo_path/builds_path as Config.Paths helpers; share hex/mix/npm caches via env vars (already done: .aiur-hex/.aiur-mix/.aiur-npm-cache).

Test fixtures leak into real state: ~/.aiur/repo has acme/widgets, test-org/test-repo, owner/repo and _unresolved dirs; ~/.cache holds many aiur-test-logs-* membership dirs.

Savings are counted in those features, not here.
features.rewrite_notes: One DurableLog (append+fsync+tail-repair) and one AtomicJSON (write-temp+rename) used by every store; tests must set the state root explicitly.
